raw_response:
Let me think this through the way I actually plan each year on my land.

---

**My thinking, field by field**

I've been farming these 12.4 mu for a long time — I know every plot. Cotton is my main cash crop, always has been around here in Quzhou. I've got about 5 mu of my better, flatter land set aside for cotton every year. Then I've got 4 mu where I run wheat in winter and maize right after in summer — that's my grain, keeps the family fed and we sell what's left. The remaining 3.4 mu is sandier ground on the edge — I put peanut on about 2 mu there and mung bean on the last 1.4 mu. Peanut sells for decent money and mung bean doesn't need much water, good to have something that won't die if the rains come late.

With 6 people in the household but some of the young ones working off-farm in town, I've basically got me, my wife, and sometimes one of the kids back for picking season. That's why I can't plant more cotton — picking is what limits me. Hired labor at picking time costs 100+ yuan a day now, and it eats into what I make.

**Cotton (5 mu).** I'll plant late April once the soil is warm enough, around the 20th if the weather holds. I buy the Bt hybrid seed from the shop in town — about 50 yuan a mu, but it saves me spraying for bollworm three or four times, so it's worth it. I lay plastic mulch, plow the base fertilizer under before planting. Total N about 15 kg per mu — I put compound fertilizer as base, then topdress urea at squaring and again at flowering if the plants look right. I'll irrigate twice from the well, once at squaring in mid-July and once at flowering if it's dry. Pesticide — I spray for aphids early, and usually for spider mites in August. The extension guy says to use less N but honestly I've tried it and yield drops, so I stick with what works. Last year I got about 260 kg lint per mu, should be similar this year.

**Wheat (4 mu).** Already planted last October, will be harvested early June. I used about 15 kg N per mu total — most of it as base compound, topdressed urea at jointing in March. One winter irrigation, one at jointing, probably one more at grain filling. Sprayed herbicide once in spring. Expect around 400 kg per mu.

**Maize (4 mu, after wheat).** Tight window — I need to plant within 3-5 days of wheat harvest, around June 10-15. No-till direct seeding with a hired planter. Hybrid seed, 40 yuan a mu. About 14 kg N per mu — base compound at planting, topdress urea at the big trumpet stage late July. One irrigation if rains don't come in July. Spray herbicide right after planting. Usually get around 450 kg per mu.

**Peanut (2 mu).** Sandier ground suits peanut fine. Plant early May, harvest September. Seed is expensive — maybe 60 yuan per mu since I buy fresh most years. I don't put much N because peanut makes its own, but I do put phosphorus and potassium — about 6 kg each as compound fertilizer. Irrigate once at flowering. Sometimes spray for leaf spot in August. Get about 250 kg per mu of shelled peanut.

**Mung bean (1.4 mu).** Goes on the smallest plot. Plant late May or early June. Very little input — maybe 40 yuan of compound fertilizer for the whole plot, barely any water, no real pesticide. Short season, ready by September. 100 kg per mu is decent.

**On money.** Cotton soaks up most of the input budget because of the seed, plastic, and sprays. Total inputs come to around 4,200 yuan across everything. I keep some cash back for emergencies and for the hired picker at cotton harvest.
